newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Jan-July trade surplus widens to $14.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Russia Jan-July trade surplus widens to $14.3 bln.

text.p: Russia posted a trade surplus of $14.3 billion in the first seven months of this year after a $13.4 billion surplus in the same period of 1995, the State Statistic Committee said.
According to preliminary data the trade surplus in the first
eight months of this year was $15.8 billion, up from $15.0
billion in the first eight months of 1995.
RUSSIAN MERCHANDISE TRADE Jan-July96 Jan-June96 Jan-July95
RUSSIAN MERCHANDISE TRADE July 96 June 96 July 95

Notes - Figures in billion dollars, FOB. Data are for trade with Russia's "far abroad" excluding former Soviet states. Including trade with CIS countries, the surplus in the first seven months narrowed to $13.5 billion from $13.7 billion last year.
The Ministry of Foreign Economic Relations previously issued figures which did not include imports by small "shuttle" traders. The ministry's export data were the same as the statistics committee's.
The ministry said imports in January-July totalled $18.6 billion, with the surplus widening to $20.3 billion from $18.6 billion last year. --Konstantin Kutsyllo, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
